f: What is a كَلِمَةٌ in Arabic grammar?
b: A كَلِمَةٌ is a single utterance (قَوْلٌ مُفْرَدٌ) that denotes one word in grammatical terminology.

f: How does the linguistic meaning of كَلِمَةٌ differ from its grammatical meaning?
b: Linguistically, كَلِمَةٌ may refer to a complete meaningful statement. Grammatically, it refers to a single word (قَوْلٌ مُفْرَدٌ).

f: What is meant by قَوْلٌ in the definition of كَلِمَةٌ?
b: قَوْلٌ is a spoken expression (لَفْظٌ) that conveys a meaning.

f: What is لَفْظٌ?
b: لَفْظٌ is a sound composed of letters, whether or not it carries meaning.

f: Is every لَفْظٌ considered قَوْلًا?
b: No. Every قَوْلٌ is a لَفْظٌ, but not every لَفْظٌ is a قَوْلٌ, because some utterances have no meaning.

f: What does مُفْرَدٌ mean in the definition of كَلِمَةٌ?
b: مُفْرَدٌ is something whose individual parts do not indicate parts of its meaning.

f: Why is غُلَامُ زَيْدٍ not considered مُفْرَدًا?
b: Because each component (غُلَامٌ and زَيْدٌ) contributes part of the overall meaning, making it مُرَكَّبًا.

f: Why does Ibn Hishām define كَلِمَةٌ using قَوْلٌ instead of لَفْظٌ?
b: Because قَوْلٌ applies only to meaningful utterances, whereas لَفْظٌ also includes meaningless sounds. Using قَوْلٌ makes the definition more precise.

f: Into how many categories is كَلِمَةٌ divided?
b: كَلِمَةٌ has three categories: اِسْمٌ, فِعْلٌ, and حَرْفٌ.

f: How was it established that there are only three categories of كَلِمَةٌ?
b: Through الِاسْتِقْرَاءُ (inductive examination) of Arabic speech by grammarians.

f: What are the three principal signs of an اِسْمٌ mentioned by Ibn Hishām?
b: An اِسْمٌ is recognized by accepting الـ, accepting التَّنْوِينُ, or by being something about which a statement can be made (الْحَدِيثُ عَنْهُ).

f: What is التَّنْوِينُ?
b: التَّنْوِينُ is an additional silent ن pronounced at the end of a word but not written, and it is not for emphasis.

f: Which sign of an اِسْمٌ does Ibn Hishām consider the most useful?
b: الْحَدِيثُ عَنْهُ (being the subject about which something is predicated).

f: Why is the ت in ضَرَبْتُ considered an اِسْمٌ?
b: Because it can function as the entity about which a statement is made (الْحَدِيثُ عَنْهُ), even though it does not accept الـ or التَّنْوِينُ.

f: Into what two categories are أَسْمَاءُ divided?
b: They are divided into مُعْرَبٌ and مَبْنِيٌّ.

f: What is a مُعْرَبٌ?
b: A مُعْرَبٌ is a noun whose ending changes because of governing factors (الْعَوَامِلُ).

f: What is a مَبْنِيٌّ?
b: A مَبْنِيٌّ is a noun whose ending remains fixed regardless of the governing factors.

f: Does every change at the end of a word count as إِعْرَابٌ?
b: No. Only changes caused by grammatical governing factors (الْعَوَامِلُ) are إِعْرَابٌ.

f: What are the four types of بِنَاءٌ?
b: الْبِنَاءُ may be on الْكَسْرُ, الْفَتْحُ, الضَّمُّ, or السُّكُونُ.

f: How do the people of Ḥijāz decline feminine proper names on the pattern فَعَالِ (e.g. حَذَامِ)?
b: The people of Ḥijāz treat them as مَبْنِيٌّ عَلَى الْكَسْرِ (indeclinable with a fixed kasrah) in all grammatical positions.

f: How do the tribes of Banū Tamīm treat feminine proper names such as حَذَامُ and قَطَامُ?
b: They have two major usages: (1) some decline them as مَمْنُوعٌ مِنَ الصَّرْفِ (ḍammah in the nominative and fatḥah in the accusative and genitive); (2) the more common view distinguishes between names ending in ر and those that do not.

f: How does the majority of Banū Tamīm distinguish between feminine names ending in ر and those that do not?
b: Names ending in ر (e.g. وَبَارِ and حَضَارِ) are treated like the Ḥijāzīs and built on kasrah, while names not ending in ر (e.g. حَذَامُ and قَطَامُ) are declined as مَمْنُوعٌ مِنَ الصَّرْفِ.

f: How do the people of Ḥijāz treat أَمْسِ when it refers to "yesterday"?
b: They treat أَمْسِ as مَبْنِيٌّ عَلَى الْكَسْرِ in every grammatical position.

f: How do the tribes of Banū Tamīm treat أَمْسُ?
b: Two usages exist: some decline it as مَمْنُوعٌ مِنَ الصَّرْفِ (ḍammah in the nominative, fatḥah otherwise), while others make it nominative with ḍammah but build it on kasrah in the accusative and genitive.

f: Does Ibn Hishām accept the opinion that some Arabs build أَمْسَ on fatḥah?
b: No. He considers this opinion mistaken and prefers the explanation that the cited form is actually the declined مَمْنُوعٌ مِنَ الصَّرْفِ form.

f: Which compound numerals are مَبْنِيٌّ عَلَى الْفَتْحِ?
b: أَحَدَ عَشَرَ and its sisters are built on fatḥah in all cases, except that the first part of اثْنَا عَشَرَ

f: How is اثْنَا عَشَرَ different from the other compound numerals?
b: Its first component (اثْنَا

f: Under what condition are قَبْلُ and بَعْدُ built on ḍammah?
b: They are built on ḍammah when the مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ is omitted while its meaning is still intended (حُذِفَ الْمُضَافُ إِلَيْهِ وَنُوِيَ مَعْنَاهُ).

f: What are the four grammatical states of قَبْلُ and بَعْدُ?
b: (1) Added to a visible مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ; (2) the مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ is omitted but its wording is intended; (3) the مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ is omitted and not intended; (4) the مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ is omitted while only its meaning is intended, in which case they are built on ḍammah.

f: How are قَبْلَ and بَعْدَ parsed when followed by an explicit مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ?
b: They are fully declined (مُعْرَبَانِ): usually accusative as adverbs of time/place (ظَرْفٌ) or genitive after مِنْ.

f: How are قَبْلِ and بَعْدِ treated when the مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ is omitted but its wording is intended?
b: They remain declined but do not take tanwīn because the omitted إِضَافَة is still intended.

f: How are قَبْلًا and بَعْدًا treated when the omitted مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ is neither mentioned nor intended?
b: They are fully declined and take تَنْوِينٌ, because they function as complete indefinite nouns.

f: Which words are included in the expression "وَأَخَوَاتُهَا" when discussing قَبْلُ and بَعْدُ?
b: It includes the six direction nouns (أَسْمَاءُ الْجِهَاتِ السِّتُّ) and similar words such as أَوَّلُ and دُونُ.

f: Which common particles are given as examples of words مَبْنِيَّةٌ عَلَى السُّكُونِ?
b: Ibn Hishām gives مَنْ and كَمْ as examples of words built on sukūn.

f: Does the grammatical position of مَنْ affect its ending?
b: No. مَنْ remains مَبْنِيٌّ عَلَى السُّكُونِ regardless of whether it is nominative, accusative, or genitive.

f: Can كَمْ occupy different grammatical positions while remaining unchanged?
b: Yes. It may be nominative, accusative, or genitive, but it remains مَبْنِيٌّ عَلَى السُّكُونِ.

f: Why does Ibn Hishām mention words built on السُّكُونُ last?
b: To prevent the misconception that building on sukūn is exceptional; he emphasizes that السُّكُونُ أَصْلُ الْبِنَاءِ (sukūn is the original form of indeclinability).

f: Into what three categories is الْفِعْلُ divided?
b: الْفِعْلُ is divided into فِعْلٌ مَاضٍ, فِعْلُ الْأَمْرِ, and الْفِعْلُ الْمُضَارِعُ.

f: How is فِعْلٌ مَاضٍ recognized?
b: A فِعْلٌ مَاضٍ is recognized by its ability to accept تَاءُ التَّأْنِيثِ السَّاكِنَةُ.

f: What is the basic rule for the building (بِنَاء) of فِعْلٌ مَاضٍ?
b: A فِعْلٌ مَاضٍ is basically مَبْنِيٌّ عَلَى الْفَتْحِ.

f: When is فِعْلٌ مَاضٍ built on ḍammah or sukūn instead of fatḥah?
b: It is built on ḍammah when attached to وَاوُ الْجَمَاعَةِ, and on sukūn when attached to a moving nominative pronoun (الضَّمِيرُ الْمَرْفُوعُ الْمُتَحَرِّكُ).

f: What are the three possible building states of فِعْلٌ مَاضٍ?
b: It may be built on الْفَتْحُ, الضَّمُّ, or السُّكُونُ.

f: Which four words does Ibn Hishām consider to be verbs despite scholarly disagreement?
b: He considers نِعْمَ, بِئْسَ, عَسَى, and لَيْسَ to be verbs.

f: What evidence does Ibn Hishām give that نِعْمَ, بِئْسَ, عَسَى, and لَيْسَ are verbs?
b: They accept تَاءُ التَّأْنِيثِ السَّاكِنَةُ, which is a sign of the past tense verb.

f: How is فِعْلُ الْأَمْرِ recognized?
b: It is recognized by combining two conditions: it indicates a command (الطَّلَبُ) and accepts يَاءُ الْمُخَاطَبَةِ.

f: Why are words like صَهْ and مَهْ not considered فِعْلُ الْأَمْرِ?
b: Although they indicate a command, they do not accept يَاءُ الْمُخَاطَبَةِ.

f: Why are forms such as تَقُومِينَ not considered فِعْلُ الْأَمْرِ?
b: Although they accept يَاءُ الْمُخَاطَبَةِ, they do not express a command.

f: What is the basic rule for the building (بِنَاء) of فِعْلُ الْأَمْرِ?
b: فِعْلُ الْأَمْرِ is basically مَبْنِيٌّ عَلَى السُّكُونِ.

f: When is فِعْلُ الْأَمْرِ built by deleting its final letter?
b: When it is مُعْتَلُّ الْآخِرِ (ends with a weak letter).

f: When is فِعْلُ الْأَمْرِ built by deleting the nūn?
b: When it is attached to أَلِفُ الِاثْنَيْنِ, وَاوُ الْجَمَاعَةِ, or يَاءُ الْمُخَاطَبَةِ.

f: What are the three possible building states of فِعْلُ الْأَمْرِ?
b: It may be built on السُّكُونُ, deletion of the final weak letter (حَذْفُ الْآخِرِ), or deletion of the nūn (حَذْفُ النُّونِ).

f: What is the grammatical status of هَلُمَّ in the dialect of Ḥijāz?
b: It is اِسْمُ فِعْلٍ because it indicates a command but does not accept يَاءُ الْمُخَاطَبَةِ.

f: What is the grammatical status of هَلُمَّ in the dialect of Banū Tamīm?
b: It is فِعْلُ أَمْرٍ because it both expresses a command and accepts يَاءُ الْمُخَاطَبَةِ.

f: How does هَلُمَّ differ in usage between the dialects of Ḥijāz and Banū Tamīm?
b: In Ḥijāz, it has one fixed form regardless of the addressee. In Banū Tamīm, it changes according to the attached pronoun like an imperative verb.

f: Can هَلُمَّ be used both transitively and intransitively?
b: Yes. Ibn Hishām cites Qur'ānic evidence that it is used both ways.

f: Are هَاتِ and تَعَالَ considered imperative verbs?
b: Yes. Ibn Hishām considers both to be فِعْلُ أَمْرٍ because they indicate a command and accept يَاءُ الْمُخَاطَبَةِ.

f: How is the final letter of هَاتِ inflected?
b: The final ت is always kasrah except with the masculine plural, where it takes ḍammah.

f: How is the final letter of تَعَالَ inflected?
b: The final ل always remains fatḥah in every form.

f: Why is the expression تَعَالِي أُقَاسِمُكِ الْهُمُومَ (with kasrah on the ل) considered incorrect?
b: Because the ل of تَعَالَ remains fatḥah in all forms; the correct form is تَعَالَيْ.

f: How is الْفِعْلُ الْمُضَارِعُ recognized?
b: It is recognized by accepting لَمْ and by beginning with one of the letters of نَأَيْتُ (أ، ن، ي، ت).

f: How is the first letter of الْفِعْلُ الْمُضَارِعُ vowelized?
b: It takes ḍammah if its past tense is quadriliteral (رُبَاعِيٌّ); otherwise it normally takes fatḥah.

f: When is الْفِعْلُ الْمُضَارِعُ built rather than declined?
b: It is built on sukūn with نُونُ النِّسْوَةِ, and on fatḥah when directly attached to نُونُ التَّوْكِيدِ. Otherwise, it is مُعْرَبٌ.

f: What is the primary sign by which الْفِعْلُ الْمُضَارِعُ is recognized?
b: The essential sign of الْفِعْلُ الْمُضَارِعُ is that it accepts the particle لَمْ.

f: Are the letters نَأَيْتُ by themselves sufficient to identify الْفِعْلُ الْمُضَارِعُ?
b: No. Although every فِعْلٌ مُضَارِعٌ begins with one of the letters ن، أ، ي، ت, these letters alone are not sufficient because they may also occur at the beginning of past tense verbs.

f: What are أَحْرُفُ الْمُضَارَعَةِ?
b: أَحْرُفُ الْمُضَارَعَةِ are the four letters ن، أ، ي، ت, which appear at the beginning of the present tense verb.

f: Why does Ibn Hishām mention أَحْرُفُ الْمُضَارَعَةِ if they are not the defining sign of الْمُضَارِعُ?
b: He mentions them only as a preparation for the rules governing the beginning of the present tense verb, not as its primary definition.

f: How is the first letter of الْفِعْلُ الْمُضَارِعُ vowelized according to the form of the past tense?
b: It takes ḍammah if the past tense is quadriliteral (رُبَاعِيٌّ) and fatḥah if the past tense has fewer or more than four letters.

f: Into how many grammatical states does the ending of الْفِعْلُ الْمُضَارِعُ fall?
b: The ending of الْفِعْلُ الْمُضَارِعُ has three states: it may be built on السُّكُونُ, built on الْفَتْحُ, or be مُعْرَبٌ.

f: When is الْفِعْلُ الْمُضَارِعُ built on sukūn?
b: It is built on sukūn when attached to نُونُ النِّسْوَةِ.

f: Why is يَعْفُونَ ("the men pardon") different from يَعْفُونَ in إِلَّا أَنْ يَعْفُونَ?
b: In إِلَّا أَنْ يَعْفُونَ, the و is an original root letter from عَفَا, so the verb is built on sukūn because of نُونُ النِّسْوَةِ. In الرِّجَالُ يَعْفُونَ, the و is the plural pronoun (وَاوُ الْجَمَاعَةِ), and the verb is declinable.

f: When is الْفِعْلُ الْمُضَارِعُ built on fatḥah?
b: It is built on fatḥah when it is directly attached to نُونُ التَّوْكِيدِ (مُبَاشَرَةً).

f: What does Ibn Hishām mean by the requirement that نُونُ التَّوْكِيدِ be "مُبَاشِرَةٌ"?
b: There must be no overt or implied separator between the verb and نُونُ التَّوْكِيدِ.

f: Why are verbs such as لَا تَتَّبِعَانِّ, لَتُبْلَوُنَّ, and فَإِمَّا تَرَيِنَّ still مُعْرَبَةً?
b: Because a pronoun (أَلِفُ الِاثْنَيْنِ, وَاوُ الْجَمَاعَةِ, or يَاءُ الْمُخَاطَبَةِ) separates the verb from نُونُ التَّوْكِيدِ, so the nūn is not directly attached.

f: Can a present tense verb remain مُعْرَبًا even when نُونُ التَّوْكِيدِ appears directly after it in pronunciation?
b: Yes. If there is an implied separator (such as a deleted نُونُ الرَّفْعِ), the verb is still considered مُعْرَبًا.

f: In which situations is الْفِعْلُ الْمُضَارِعُ مُعْرَبًا?
b: It is مُعْرَبٌ in every situation except when attached to نُونُ النِّسْوَةِ or directly attached to نُونُ التَّوْكِيدِ.

f: How is الْحَرْفُ recognized?
b: الْحَرْفُ is recognized by not accepting any of the signs of either الِاسْمُ or الْفِعْلُ.

f: Why are هَلْ and بَلْ classified as حُرُوفٌ?
b: They accept none of the signs of nouns or verbs; since كَلِمَةٌ has only three categories, they must therefore be حُرُوفٌ.

f: Which four particles does Ibn Hishām specifically mention because scholars disagreed about their classification?
b: He discusses إِذْمَا, مَهْمَا, مَا الْمَصْدَرِيَّةُ, and لَمَّا الرَّابِطَةُ.

f: What is Ibn Hishām's preferred classification of إِذْمَا?
b: Following Sībawayh, he regards إِذْمَا as a حَرْفٌ like the conditional particle إِنْ, rather than a temporal noun.

f: What is the majority opinion regarding مَهْمَا?
b: The majority regard مَهْمَا as an اِسْمٌ, because pronouns may refer back to it, and pronouns only refer to nouns.

f: What evidence do the majority use to show that مَهْمَا is an اِسْمٌ?
b: In the verse ﴿مَهْمَا تَأْتِنَا بِهِ مِنْ آيَةٍ﴾, the pronoun ـهِ refers back to مَهْمَا, and pronouns refer only to nouns.

f: What is Ibn Hishām's preferred opinion regarding مَهْمَا?
b: Ibn Hishām concludes that مَهْمَا is an اِسْمٌ, not a حَرْفٌ. Its subject is an implied pronoun, while the following phrase explains (يُفَسِّرُ) مَهْمَا.

f: How does Ibn Hishām explain the construction of مَهْمَا تَكُنْ مِنْ خَلِيقَةٍ?
b: The subject of تَكُنْ is an implied pronoun referring to مَهْمَا, while مِنْ خَلِيقَةٍ explains the meaning of مَهْمَا rather than serving as its grammatical subject.

f: What is مَا الْمَصْدَرِيَّةُ?
b: مَا الْمَصْدَرِيَّةُ is مَا that combines with what follows it to form a verbal noun (مَصْدَرٌ).

f: How does مَا الْمَصْدَرِيَّةُ function in a sentence?
b: It converts the following clause into a verbal noun that can be interpreted as a single noun phrase.

f: What is Ibn Hishām's preferred opinion regarding مَا الْمَصْدَرِيَّةُ?
b: Following Sībawayh, he considers مَا الْمَصْدَرِيَّةُ to be a حَرْفٌ, like أَنْ الْمَصْدَرِيَّةُ.

f: What opinion does الأَخْفَشُ hold regarding مَا الْمَصْدَرِيَّةُ?
b: الأَخْفَشُ and ابن السَّرَّاج considered it an اِسْمٌ meaning "الَّذِي", referring to the action or event.

f: What argument does Ibn Hishām use against treating مَا الْمَصْدَرِيَّةُ as an اِسْمٌ?
b: If it were a relative noun (اِسْمٌ مَوْصُولٌ), ordinary expressions requiring an explicit returning pronoun would be acceptable, but they are not found in Arabic usage.

f: Into how many categories does لَمَّا fall?
b: لَمَّا has three categories: نَافِيَةٌ, إِيجَابِيَّةٌ, and رَابِطَةٌ.

f: What is لَمَّا النَّافِيَةُ?
b: It is a particle meaning "not yet," functioning like لَمْ.

f: What is لَمَّا الْإِيجَابِيَّةُ?
b: It is a particle meaning "إِلَّا" used in expressions of insistence or exhortation.

f: What is لَمَّا الرَّابِطَةُ?
b: It links the occurrence of one event to the occurrence of another.

f: What is Ibn Hishām's preferred opinion regarding لَمَّا الرَّابِطَةُ?
b: He considers لَمَّا الرَّابِطَةُ to be a حَرْفٌ, not a temporal noun (ظَرْفٌ).

f: What is the grammatical rule for الْحُرُوفُ in general?
b: Every حَرْفٌ is مَبْنِيٌّ and has no share in الإِعْرَابُ.

f: What is الْكَلَامُ according to Ibn Hishām?
b: الْكَلَامُ is a meaningful utterance (لَفْظٌ مُفِيدٌ).

f: What does لَفْظٌ mean in the definition of الْكَلَامُ?
b: It means an audible expression composed of letters, or something equivalent to one, such as an implied pronoun.

f: What does مُفِيدٌ mean in the definition of الْكَلَامُ?
b: It means that the utterance conveys a complete meaning upon which one may stop without expecting additional information.

f: Is a written expression without pronunciation considered كَلَامًا?
b: No. Writing alone is not كَلَامٌ because الْكَلَامُ requires لَفْظٌ (actual utterance).

f: Is a gesture considered كَلَامًا?
b: No. A gesture may convey meaning, but it is not لَفْظٌ, so it is not كَلَامٌ.

f: What is the minimum composition required for الْكَلَامُ?
b: The smallest complete كَلَامٌ consists of either two nouns or a verb and one noun.

f: What are the four possible forms of الْكَلَامُ composed of two nouns?
b: (1) مُبْتَدَأٌ and خَبَرٌ; (2) مُبْتَدَأٌ and a subject replacing the predicate; (3) مُبْتَدَأٌ and a deputy subject replacing the predicate; (4) اِسْمُ فِعْلٍ with its subject.

f: What are the two possible forms of الْكَلَامُ composed of a verb and one noun?
b: The noun may be either the فَاعِلٌ or نَائِبُ الْفَاعِلِ.

f: What are the two possible forms of الْكَلَامُ composed of two clauses?
b: They may consist of a شَرْطٌ with its جَزَاءٌ, or an oath with its answer (الْقَسَمُ وَجَوَابُهُ).

f: Give an example of الْكَلَامُ composed of a verb and two nouns.
b: A verb followed by two noun complements, such as with كَانَ and its predicate.

f: Give an example of الْكَلَامُ composed of a verb and three nouns.
b: A verb that takes three elements, such as عَلِمَ with its object and predicate.

f: Give an example of الْكَلَامُ composed of a verb and four nouns.
b: A causative verb such as أَعْلَمَ may take four noun elements.

f: What is Iʿrāb (الإِعْرَاب) according to Ibn Hishām?
b: الإِعْرَاب is a visible (ظَاهِر) or estimated (مُقَدَّر) grammatical ending produced by an عَامِل (governing element) at the end of a word.

f: What is the difference between visible (ظَاهِر) and estimated (مُقَدَّر) Iʿrāb?
b: Visible الإِعْرَاب appears on the word's ending. Estimated الإِعْرَاب is not pronounced because pronunciation is impossible or prevented (e.g. with الْفَتَى), but it is understood grammatically.

f: What are the four types of Iʿrāb (الإِعْرَاب) and which parts of speech can each occur in?
b: The four types are: الرَّفْعُ, النَّصْبُ, الْجَرُّ, and الْجَزْمُ. رَفْع and نَصْب occur in both nouns and verbs. جَرّ is exclusive to nouns. جَزْم is exclusive to verbs.

f: What are the original (أَصْلِيَّة) signs of the four types of Iʿrāb?
b: The original signs are: الضَّمَّةُ for الرَّفْعُ, الْفَتْحَةُ for النَّصْبُ, الْكَسْرَةُ for الْجَرُّ, and حَذْفُ الْحَرَكَةِ (السُّكُون) for الْجَزْمُ. Other signs are secondary (فَرْعِيَّة).

f: How are the secondary (فَرْعِيَّة) signs of Iʿrāb organized?
b: The secondary signs are discussed in seven chapters: five dealing with nouns and two dealing with verbs.

f: What are the six nouns (الأَسْمَاءُ السِّتَّةُ), and how are they declined?
b: The six nouns are أَبٌ، أَخٌ، حَمٌ، هَنٌ، فُو، ذُو (بمعنى صاحب). When their conditions are fulfilled, they are declined with letters: وَاو for رَفْع, أَلِف for نَصْب, and يَاء for جَرّ.

f: What are the conditions for the six nouns (الأَسْمَاءُ السِّتَّةُ) to be declined by letters instead of vowel signs?
b: They must be (1) singular (مُفْرَدَة), (2) not diminutive (مُكَبَّرَة), (3) in an إِضَافَة construction, and (4) the مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ must not be يَاءُ الْمُتَكَلِّمِ.

f: How are the six nouns declined if one of the required conditions is not fulfilled?
b: They return to the normal declension with vowel signs. This happens, for example, if they are dual, broken plural, diminutive, or not in إِضَافَة.

f: How are the six nouns declined when they are dual or sound plurals?
b: If made dual, they follow the normal rules of the dual. If made sound masculine plurals (possible only for أَب، أَخ، حَم), they follow the normal sound masculine plural rules.

f: How are the six nouns declined when they are attached to Yāʾ al-Mutakallim (يَاءُ الْمُتَكَلِّمِ)?
b: They no longer take the letter endings. Instead, they have estimated (مُقَدَّر) vowel signs, while their final form remains with kasrah because of the attached يَاء.

f: What does the noun حَمٌ mean among the six nouns?
b: حَمٌ primarily refers to the husband's male relatives, such as his father, uncle, and cousin, though it is sometimes also used for the wife's relatives.

f: What is the meaning of هَنٌ according to Ibn Hishām?
b: Scholars differed: it may be a generic substitute word, a euphemism for something indecent to mention, or specifically a euphemism for the private parts.

f: What is the preferred way to use هَنٌ when it is not in an Iḍāfah construction?
b: The preferred usage is to treat it like غَدٌ: it is defective (مَنْقُوص) and declined with ordinary vowel signs rather than the special letter endings.

f: How is هَنٌ treated when it is in an Iḍāfah construction?
b: The majority of Arabs still decline it with ordinary vowel signs (هَنُكَ، هَنَكَ، هَنِكَ). A less common dialect, reported by سِيبَوَيْهِ, declines it like the other six nouns using وَاو، أَلِف، يَاء.

f: How is the dual noun (المثنى), such as الزيدان, declined?
b: The dual is nominative with alif (ـان) in place of ḍammah, and accusative and genitive with yāʾ (ـين) in place of fatḥah and kasrah. Example: جاء الزيدان، رأيت الزيدين، مررت بالزيدين.

f: Which words are treated like the dual (المثنى) in declension?
b: Four expressions are treated like the dual: كلا، كلتا (when attached to a pronoun), and اثنان، اثنتان (in all cases).

f: Under what condition are كلا and كلتا declined like the dual?
b: They are declined like the dual only when attached to a pronoun, such as كلاهما and كلتيهما.

f: How are كلا and كلتا declined when attached to a pronoun?
b: They are nominative with alif and accusative and genitive with yāʾ, just like the dual. Examples: جاء كلاهما، رأيت كليهما، مررت بكليهما.

f: How are كلا and كلتا declined when attached to an explicit noun instead of a pronoun?
b: They remain with alif in all three cases, and their case endings are estimated (muqaddarah) because they are maqṣūr nouns. Example: جاء كلا أخويك، رأيت كلا أخويك، مررت بكلا أخويك.

f: How are اثنان and اثنتان declined?
b: They are declined exactly like the dual whether they are independent, attached to a pronoun, attached to an explicit noun, or compounded with عشر.

f: How are اثنان and اثنتان declined when compounded with عشر (e.g., اثنا عشر)?
b: They still follow the dual: اثنا عشر in the nominative, and اثني عشر in the accusative and genitive.

f: How is the sound masculine plural (جمع المذكر السالم), such as الزيدون, declined?
b: It is nominative with wāw (ـون) and accusative and genitive with yāʾ (ـين). Example: جاء الزيدون، رأيت الزيدين، مررت بالزيدين.

f: Which words are treated like the sound masculine plural (جمع المذكر السالم) in declension?
b: They include أولو, the numerals عشرون through تسعون, أهلون، وابلون، أرضون، سنون and its class, بنون, عليون, and any plural form that has become a proper name.

f: How is أولو declined?
b: It is declined like the sound masculine plural: أولو (nominative), أولي (accusative and genitive).

f: How are the numerals عشرون through تسعون declined?
b: They are declined like the sound masculine plural: wāw in the nominative and yāʾ in the accusative and genitive. Example: جاء عشرون، رأيت عشرين، مررت بعشرين.

f: How is أهلون declined?
b: It is declined like the sound masculine plural: أهلون (nominative), أهلين (accusative and genitive).

f: Which nouns belong to the class of سنون that are declined like the sound masculine plural?
b: Every triliteral noun whose final radical has been omitted, replaced by tāʾ al-taʾnīth, and which is not a broken plural. Examples include سنون، عضون، عزون، ثبون، قلون.

f: Why are words like سنون declined like the sound masculine plural?
b: Because the Arabs compensated for the omitted final radical by giving the broken plural the outward form of the sound masculine plural (ending in ـون/ـين).

f: How is بنون declined?
b: بنون is declined like the sound masculine plural, despite not being one originally.

f: Why is عليون declined like the sound masculine plural?
b: Because عليون was originally a plural of علي, then became a proper noun (the highest place in Paradise), yet retained the declension of its original plural form.

f: How is a plural form that has become a proper name (e.g., زيدون used as a man's name) declined?
b: It continues to be declined like the sound masculine plural: زيدون، زيدين، زيدين.

f: How is a plural formed with an additional alif and tāʾ (جمع بألف وتاء مزيدتين), such as هندات, declined?
b: It is accusative with kasrah instead of fatḥah, while remaining nominative with ḍammah and genitive with kasrah.

f: Does the rule of taking kasrah in the accusative apply only to feminine nouns?
b: No. It applies to every plural formed with an additional alif and tāʾ, whether the singular is feminine or masculine.

f: Does the rule of taking kasrah in the accusative depend on the singular remaining unchanged?
b: No. It applies whether the singular's form remains unchanged or undergoes changes when pluralized.

f: Why does Ibn Hishām prefer the expression "a plural formed with an additional alif and tāʾ" instead of "sound feminine plural"?
b: Because his wording includes feminine and masculine nouns alike, whether the singular remains unchanged or changes in form, making it more comprehensive.

f: Why are words such as أبيات and أموات not included among the plurals that take kasrah in the accusative?
b: Because the tāʾ in these words is original, not additional; therefore they follow the normal rule and take fatḥah in the accusative.

f: Why are words such as قضاة and غزاة not included among the plurals that take kasrah in the accusative?
b: Because although the tāʾ is additional, the alif is original (resulting from the transformation of wāw or yāʾ), so they follow the normal rule and take fatḥah in the accusative.

f: How is the diptote (ما لا ينصرف) declined in the genitive?
b: A diptote takes fatḥah instead of kasrah in the genitive, e.g. مررت بأفضلَ منك, unless it has al- or is in iḍāfah, in which case it takes kasrah, e.g. بالأفضل، بأفضلكم.

f: What is a diptote (ما لا ينصرف)?
b: A diptote is a noun prevented from tanwīn and from taking kasrah in the genitive because it has two secondary causes (علتان فرعيتان) from the nine recognized causes, or one cause that is equivalent to two.

f: What is an example of a diptote having two secondary causes?
b: فاطمة is a diptote because it combines definiteness (proper noun) and femininity, both of which are secondary causes.

f: What is an example of a diptote having one cause equivalent to two?
b: Plurals on the patterns مفاعل and مفاعيل (e.g. مساجد، مصابيح) are diptotes because the ending pattern (صيغة منتهى الجموع) alone counts as a cause equivalent to two.

f: What is meant by صيغة منتهى الجموع (the ultimate plural pattern)?
b: It refers to the plural patterns مفاعل and مفاعيل, which the Arabs regarded as the final stage of plural formation, since such plurals are not themselves pluralized again.

f: Why is صيغة منتهى الجموع considered equivalent to two causes?
b: Because it represents the final and most complete form of pluralization, making it exceptionally removed from the singular and therefore strong enough to prevent declension by itself.

f: Why are words such as صحراء and حبلى diptotes?
b: Because they have permanent feminine endings, whose permanence is treated as though they possess an additional cause beyond ordinary femininity.

f: How is a diptote declined in the genitive?
b: It takes fatḥah instead of kasrah in the genitive. Example: مررت بفاطمة، بمساجد، بمصابيح، بصحراء.

f: When does a diptote return to taking kasrah in the genitive?
b: It takes kasrah when it is preceded by ال or when it is in the construct state (iḍāfah).

f: Give an example of a diptote taking kasrah because of ال.
b: وأنتم عاكفون في المساجد — المساجد is genitive with kasrah because it has ال.

f: Give an example of a diptote taking kasrah because of iḍāfah.
b: في أحسنِ تقويمٍ — أحسن is genitive with kasrah because it is annexed (muḍāf).

f: Why does Ibn Hishām prefer the example بأفضلكم over بعثماننا when illustrating a diptote in iḍāfah?
b: Because أفضل remains a diptote after annexation, whereas عثمان may lose one of its causes (proper noun status) when treated as indefinite before annexation, making it a weaker example.

f: What are the Five Verbs (الأفعال الخمسة)?
b: They are every present-tense verb attached to the dual alif, the masculine plural wāw, or the feminine singular yāʾ: يفعلان، تفعلان، يفعلون، تفعلون، تفعلين.

f: Why are these verbs called the Five Verbs (الأفعال الخمسة)?
b: Because they consist of the five present-tense forms ending with the dual alif, the plural wāw, or the feminine yāʾ.

f: How are the Five Verbs (الأفعال الخمسة) marked in the nominative?
b: They are nominative by the retention of the nūn (ثبوت النون) instead of ḍammah.

f: How are the Five Verbs (الأفعال الخمسة) marked in the accusative?
b: They are accusative by deleting the nūn (حذف النون) instead of fatḥah.

f: How are the Five Verbs (الأفعال الخمسة) marked in the jussive?
b: They are jussive by deleting the nūn (حذف النون) instead of sukūn.

f: Give an example showing the Three cases of one of the Five Verbs.
b: أنتم تقومون (nominative), لن تقوموا (accusative), لم تقوموا (jussive). The latter two delete the nūn.

f: How is a weak-final present verb (الفعل المضارع المعتل الآخر) made jussive?
b: It is made jussive by deleting its final weak letter.

f: Give examples of weak-final present verbs in the jussive.
b: لم يغز، لم يخش، لم يرم.

f: How many categories of words have estimated (implicit) case endings according to Ibn Hishām?
b: Five categories.

f: Which nouns have all three case endings estimated because the final letter cannot accept vowels?
b: Maqṣūr nouns (الاسم المقصور) ending in a permanent alif, such as الفتى.

f: Why are all three case endings estimated on maqṣūr nouns?
b: Because the final alif cannot accept any vowel.

f: Which nouns have all three case endings estimated because of attachment to another word?
b: Nouns annexed to the first-person possessive yāʾ (ياء المتكلم), such as غلامي، أبي، أخي.

f: Why are all three case endings estimated on nouns annexed to ياء المتكلم?
b: Because the required kasrah before ياء المتكلم prevents the normal case endings from appearing.

f: Which nouns have only the nominative and genitive endings estimated?
b: Manqūṣ nouns (الاسم المنقوص), such as القاضي and الداعي.

f: Why are only the nominative and genitive endings estimated on manqūṣ nouns?
b: Because ḍammah and kasrah are considered too heavy (للاستثقال) on the final yāʾ, while fatḥah is light enough to appear.

f: Which present verbs have both the nominative and accusative endings estimated?
b: Present verbs ending in alif, such as يخشى.

f: Why are the nominative and accusative endings estimated on present verbs ending in alif?
b: Because alif cannot accept vowels, making both ḍammah and fatḥah impossible to pronounce.

f: Which present verbs have only the nominative ending estimated?
b: Present verbs ending in wāw (e.g. يدعو) or yāʾ (e.g. يرمي).

f: Why is only the nominative ending estimated on present verbs ending in wāw or yāʾ?
b: Because ḍammah is heavy on these letters, whereas fatḥah is light enough to appear.

f: Does fatḥah appear on verbs ending in wāw or yāʾ?
b: Yes. Ibn Hishām states that fatḥah appears because it is light, e.g. لن يقضي، لن يدعو.

f: What causes a present tense verb (الفعل المضارع) to be in the indicative (مرفوع) state?
b: A present tense verb is indicative when it is free from both a subjunctive particle (ناصب) and a jussive particle (جازم), e.g. يقوم زيد.

f: What are the four opinions regarding what raises (يرفع) the present tense verb? Which opinion does Ibn Hishām prefer?
b: (1) Al-Farrāʾ: its being free from a nāṣib and jāzim. (2) Al-Kisāʾī: the prefix letters of the present tense. (3) Thaʿlab: its resemblance to nouns. (4) The Baṣrans: its occupying the position of a noun. Ibn Hishām prefers the first opinion: the verb is raised because it is free from both a nāṣib and a jāzim.

f: How does Ibn Hishām refute the opinion that the present-tense prefix letters are what raise the verb?
b: Because a part of a word cannot govern (work upon) the word itself.

f: How does Ibn Hishām refute the opinion that resemblance to nouns itself raises the present tense verb?
b: Resemblance explains why the verb is declinable (معرب), but each grammatical state still requires a separate governing factor. Moreover, if resemblance alone raised it, the verb would always be indicative, which is false.

f: How does Ibn Hishām refute the Baṣran view that the verb is raised because it occupies the place of a noun?
b: There are cases such as هلا يقوم where the verb is indicative even though a noun cannot occur after the particle of exhortation (هلا).

f: How many particles place the present tense verb in the subjunctive (منصوب) according to Ibn Hishām?
b: Four: لن، كي، إذن، أن.

f: Why does Ibn Hishām discuss the particle لن before the others?
b: Because لن always governs the subjunctive, unlike the other particles whose governing depends on conditions.

f: Why does Ibn Hishām discuss أن last although it is the principal subjunctive particle?
b: Because the discussion of أن is much longer, and because of its fundamental role in governing the subjunctive.

f: What meaning does the particle لن convey?
b: It indicates negation and future time by agreement.

f: Does the particle لن necessarily imply perpetual negation (التأبيد)?
b: No. Ibn Hishām rejects the opinion that لن necessarily implies perpetual negation.

f: Does the particle لن necessarily imply emphasis?
b: No. Ibn Hishām rejects the opinion that لن inherently adds emphasis.

f: How does Ibn Hishām demonstrate that لن does not imply perpetual negation or emphasis?
b: The statement لن أقوم may mean either "I will never stand" or "I will not stand during some future period," making it no stronger than لا أقوم in itself.

f: Can the particle لن be used for supplication (دعاء)?
b: No. Ibn Hishām rejects Ibn al-Sarrāj's opinion that it can be used for supplication.

f: How does Ibn Hishām interpret the verse: ﴿فَلَنْ أَكُونَ ظَهِيرًا لِلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾?
b: As a simple future negation—a pledge by Mūsā not to support criminals—not as a supplication.

f: Did Ibn Hishām accept the view that لن is composed of لا + أن or that it originated from لا?
b: No. He rejects both the opinion of al-Khalīl and that of al-Farrāʾ regarding its origin.

f: When does كي function as a subjunctive particle?
b: When it is masdariyyah (source-forming), equivalent to أن.

f: When is كي considered masdariyyah?
b: When it is preceded by لام either explicitly (لكي) or implicitly.

f: Give an example of كي preceded by an explicit لام.
b: لكيلا تأسوا.

f: Give an example where the لام before كي is understood rather than spoken.
b: جئتك كي تكرمني, understood as لكي تكرمني.

f: If كي is not analyzed as masdariyyah, what is it?
b: A preposition expressing purpose (التعليل), while أن is obligatorily omitted after it.

f: What is إذن according to Sībawayh?
b: A particle of answer and recompense (جواب وجزاء).

f: What opinion did al-Shalūbīn hold regarding إذن?
b: That it is always a particle of answer and recompense.

f: What opinion did Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī hold regarding إذن?
b: That it usually serves as answer and recompense, but may sometimes function merely as an answer.

f: What are the three conditions for إذن to make the present tense verb subjunctive?
b: (1) It must occur at the beginning of the statement. (2) The verb must refer to the future. (3) Nothing may intervene between إذن and the verb except an oath.

f: Why is the verb indicative in: زيد إذن أكرمه?
b: Because إذن is not sentence-initial.

f: Why is the verb indicative in response to a present event: إذن تصدق?
b: Because the verb refers to the present rather than the future.

f: What kind of separator is permitted between إذن and the verb?
b: Only an oath, e.g. إذن والله أكرمك.

f: What kinds of separators prevent إذن from governing the subjunctive?
b: Other separators such as يا زيد, adverbials like في الدار, or time expressions like يوم الجمعة.

f: Which type of أن governs the subjunctive?
b: أن المصدرية (the source-forming أن).

f: Which types of أن do not govern the subjunctive?
b: أن المفسرة and أن الزائدة.

f: What is أن المفسرة?
b: أن occurring after a clause containing the meaning of speech without using actual speech verbs, e.g. كتبت إليه أن يفعل كذا meaning "i.e., that he should do such-and-such."

f: What is أن الزائدة?
b: The extra أن occurring between an oath and لو, e.g. أقسم بالله أن لو يأتيني زيد لأكرمنه.

f: When is أن definitely the lightened form of الثقيلة (أن المخففة من الثقيلة)?
b: When it is preceded by a verb indicating certain knowledge (علم).

f: What two conditions follow when أن is the lightened form of الثقيلة?
b: (1) The following verb is indicative (not subjunctive). (2) A separator must come between أن and the verb.

f: What four separators may occur after أن المخففة from الثقيلة?
b: (1) Future particle (سـ or سوف). (2) Negation particle. (3) قد. (4) لو.

f: Give an example of each separator after أن المخففة from الثقيلة.
b: أن سيكون (future particle); أن لا يرجع (negation); أن قد يقوم (قد); أن لو يشاء الله (لو).

f: If أن is preceded by a verb of assumption (ظن), what are the two possible analyses?
b: It may be analyzed either as أن المصدرية (subjunctive) or as أن المخففة من الثقيلة (indicative).

f: When is أن omitted permissibly (إضمارًا جائزًا)?
b: After a conjunction preceded by a pure noun, e.g. ولبس عباءة وتقر عيني.

f: When is أن omitted obligatorily after لام التعليل?
b: After the lām of purpose, e.g. لتبين للناس, except in forms such as لئلا يعلم and لئلا يكون, where أن must remain explicit.

f: When is أن obligatorily omitted after ما كان?
b: In expressions such as وما كان الله ليعذبهم.

f: When is أن obligatorily omitted after حتى?
b: When حتى introduces a future action, e.g. حتى يرجع إلينا موسى.

f: When is أن obligatorily omitted after أو meaning "until"?
b: When أو means إلى, e.g. أو أدرك المنى ("until I attain my goal").

f: When is أن obligatorily omitted after أو meaning "except"?
b: When أو means إلا, as in the poetic expression أو تستقيما.

f: When is أن obligatorily omitted after فاء السببية and واو المعية?
b: When they are preceded by a pure negation or a request, e.g. لا يقضى عليهم فيموتوا, ولا تطغوا فيه فيحل, ولا تأكل السمك وتشرب اللبن.

f: If أن is preceded by a verb of assumption (ظن), how is it analyzed?
b: It may be analyzed either as أن المخففة من الثقيلة (followed by an indicative verb) or as أن المصدرية (followed by a subjunctive verb). The subjunctive analysis is stronger by analogy and more common in Arabic.

f: Why do grammarians unanimously analyze أن as subjunctive in the verse: ﴿أَحَسِبَ النَّاسُ أَنْ يُتْرَكُوا﴾?
b: Because after حسب in this context, أن is unanimously taken as أن المصدرية, making يتركوا subjunctive.

f: Why are both the indicative and subjunctive readings accepted in the verse: ﴿وَحَسِبُوا أَنْ لَا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ﴾?
b: Because أن after حسب may be interpreted either as أن المخففة من الثقيلة (indicative) or as أن المصدرية (subjunctive).

f: When must أن be interpreted as the source-forming particle (أن المصدرية)?
b: When it is preceded by neither a verb of certainty (علم) nor a verb of assumption (ظن), e.g. والذي أطمع أن يغفر لي خطيئتي.

f: How many kinds of omitted (مضمرة) أن are there?
b: Two: permissibly omitted (جائز) and obligatorily omitted (واجب).

f: When may أن be omitted after a conjunction?
b: When the conjunction follows a pure noun (اسم خالص) that is not interpreted as a verb.

f: Why is the verb منصوب in: ﴿أَوْ يُرْسِلَ رَسُولًا﴾?
b: Because أن is permissibly omitted after the conjunction أو, with the implied meaning أو أن يرسل رسولًا.

f: How is the phrase: ولبس عباءة وتقر عيني analyzed?
b: It is understood as ولبس عباءة وأن تقر عيني, with an omitted أن after the conjunction.

f: When may أن be omitted after the preposition لام?
b: After لام التعليل, لام العاقبة, اللام الزائدة, and similarly after كي when it functions as a preposition.

f: What is Lam al-Taʿlīl (لام التعليل)? Give an example.
b: The lām of purpose, e.g. لتبين للناس ("so that you may make clear to the people").

f: What is Lam al-ʿĀqibah (لام العاقبة)? Give an example.
b: The lām indicating the eventual outcome rather than intended purpose, e.g. فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدواً وحزناً. They did not pick him up for that purpose; it was merely the eventual result.

f: What is the extra lām (اللام الزائدة)? Give an example.
b: An additional lām that does not express purpose, e.g. إنما يريد الله ليذهب عنكم الرجس.

f: When must أن be explicitly stated after the lām?
b: When the following verb is preceded by لا, whether لا is negative or extra, e.g. لئلا يكون and لئلا يعلم.

f: When must أن be obligatorily omitted after the lām?
b: After لام الجحود, which follows a negated form of كان.

f: What is Lam al-Juḥūd (لام الجحود)?
b: The lām occurring after a negated form of كان, requiring an omitted أن, e.g. وما كان الله ليعذبهم.

f: Does Lam al-Juḥūd occur only after an explicitly past tense of كان?
b: No. It also occurs when كان is only past in meaning, e.g. لم يكن الله ليغفر لهم.

f: What are the three possible states of أن after the letter لام?
b: (1) Obligatory omission after لام الجحود. (2) Obligatory appearance when the verb is preceded by لا. (3) Either omission or appearance in other cases.

f: Give an example where أن may either be omitted or stated after the lām.
b: وأمرنا لنسلم or وأمرت لأن أكون.

f: Besides Lam al-Juḥūd, how many further places require the obligatory omission of أن?
b: Four: after حتى, after أو meaning إلى or إلا, after فاء السببية, and after واو المعية (under its conditions).

f: When is the verb after حتى subjunctive (منصوب)?
b: When it refers to an action that is future relative to what precedes حتى.

f: Must the verb after حتى be future relative to the time of speaking?
b: No. It only needs to be future relative to the preceding action, even if the whole event is already past.

f: Give an example where the verb after حتى is future both relative to the previous action and to the time of speaking.
b: لن نبرح عليه عاكفين حتى يرجع إلينا موسى.

f: Give an example where the verb after حتى is past relative to the speaker but future relative to the previous event.
b: وزلزلوا حتى يقول الرسول. The speech occurred after the shaking, though both are now past.

f: What are the two meanings of حتى when it governs a subjunctive verb?
b: (1) كي ("so that"). (2) إلى ("until").

f: When does حتى mean "so that" (كي)?
b: When what precedes it is the reason for what follows, e.g. أسلم حتى تدخل الجنة.

f: When does حتى mean "until" (إلى)?
b: When what follows marks the endpoint of what precedes, e.g. لن نبرح عليه عاكفين حتى يرجع إلينا موسى.

f: Can حتى carry both meanings simultaneously? Give an example.
b: Yes, e.g. فقاتلوا التي تبغي حتى تفيء إلى أمر الله, which may mean either "until it returns" or "so that it returns."

f: According to Ibn Hishām, what actually makes the verb after حتى subjunctive?
b: An obligatorily omitted أن, not حتى itself.

f: How does Ibn Hishām refute the Kūfan claim that حتى itself governs the subjunctive?
b: Because حتى already governs nouns by assigning the genitive case. One Arabic particle does not govern both nouns and verbs directly.

f: When is the verb after حتى indicative (مرفوع)?
b: When three conditions are met: (1) it is caused by what precedes it, (2) it expresses the present rather than the future, and (3) what precedes حتى is a complete clause.

f: Why is the verb not indicative in: سرت حتى تطلع الشمس?
b: Because the walking is not the cause of the sun's rising, so the first condition for the indicative is absent.

f: Can the "present" required for the indicative after حتى be either real or rhetorical?
b: Yes. It may describe an action actually happening at that moment or vividly narrate a past event as though it were occurring now.

f: Why is the verb indicative in the Qur'anic reading: ﴿حتى يقول الرسول﴾?
b: Because the verse vividly narrates a past event as though it were happening in the present (حكاية الحال).

f: Why is the verb not indicative in: سيري حتى أدخلها?
b: Because what precedes حتى is not a complete clause.

f: When does أو require an omitted أن?
b: When it means either إلى ("until") or إلا ("unless

f: Give an example of أو meaning "until" (إلى).
b: لألزمنك أو تقضيني حقي = "I will remain with you until you repay my right."

f: Give an example of أو meaning "except unless" (إلا).
b: لأقتلن الكافر أو يسلم = "I will kill the disbeliever unless he accepts Islam."

f: Why is أو in the verse: أو تستقيما understood as "except" rather than "until"?
b: Because becoming straight cannot be the endpoint of breaking the spear shafts, so إلا أن تستقيما is the only suitable meaning.

f: When does فاء السببية require an omitted أن?
b: When it is preceded by pure negation or by a verbal request.

f: What is an example of فاء السببية after pure negation?
b: لا يقضى عليهم فيموتوا or ما تأتينا فتحدثنا.

f: Why must the negation before فاء السببية be "pure" (محض)?
b: Because if the negation actually conveys affirmation, the condition is not fulfilled.

f: Why is the verb after فاء السببية indicative in: ما تزال تأتينا فتحدثنا?
b: Because ما تزال expresses affirmation (continuity), not pure negation.

f: Why is the verb after فاء السببية indicative in: ما تأتينا إلا فتحدثنا?
b: Because إلا cancels the negation, making the meaning affirmative rather than purely negative.

f: What kinds of verbal requests allow فاء السببية to require an omitted أن?
b: Commands, prohibitions, supplications, wishes, questions, exhortations, and similar verbal requests.

f: Give an example of فاء السببية after a command.
b: يا ناق سيري عنقًا فسيحًا إلى سليمان فنستريحا.

f: What are the different types of request (ṭalab) that allow a present verb after the causative فَاء (fāʾ as-sababiyyah) to be in the subjunctive (منصوب)?
b: The types are: command (الأمر), prohibition (النهي), incitement (التحضيض), wish (التمني), hope (الترجي), supplication (الدعاء), question (الاستفهام), and offer/invitation (العرض).

f: Give an example of a command causing the following present verb to be subjunctive after فَاء السَّبَبِيَّة.
b: يَا نَاقُ سِيرِي عَنْقًا فَسِيحًا إِلَى سُلَيْمَانَ فَنَسْتَرِيحَ — فَنَسْتَرِيحَ is subjunctive because it follows a command.

f: Give an example of a prohibition causing the following present verb to be subjunctive after فَاء السَّبَبِيَّة.
b: ﴿وَلَا تَطْغَوْا فِيهِ فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبِي﴾ — فَيَحِلَّ is subjunctive after a prohibition.

f: Give an example of incitement (التحضيض) causing the following present verb to be subjunctive after فَاء السَّبَبِيَّة.
b: ﴿لَوْلَا أَخَّرْتَنِي إِلَى أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ فَأَصَّدَّقَ﴾ — فَأَصَّدَّقَ is subjunctive after incitement.

f: Give an example of wishing (التمني) causing the following present verb to be subjunctive after فَاء السَّبَبِيَّة.
b: يَا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ مَعَهُمْ فَأَفُوزَ — فَأَفُوزَ is subjunctive after wishing.

f: Give an example of hope (الترجي) causing the following present verb to be subjunctive after فَاء السَّبَبِيَّة.
b: ﴿لَعَلِّي أَبْلُغُ الْأَسْبَابَ ... فَأَطَّلِعَ﴾ (one Qurʾānic reading) — فَأَطَّلِعَ is subjunctive after hope.

f: Give an example of supplication (الدعاء) causing the following present verb to be subjunctive after فَاء السَّبَبِيَّة.
b: رَبِّ وَفِّقْنِي فَلَا أَعْدِلَ عَنْ سُنَنِ السَّاعِينَ فِي خَيْرِ سُنَنٍ — فَلَا أَعْدِلَ is subjunctive after supplication.

f: Give an example of a question causing the following present verb to be subjunctive after فَاء السَّبَبِيَّة.
b: هَلْ تَعْرِفُونَ لُبَانَاتِي فَأَرْجُوَ أَنْ تُقْضَى فَيَرْتَدَّ بَعْضُ الرُّوحِ لِلْجَسَدِ — the verb after فَاء is subjunctive.

f: Give an example of an offer/invitation (العرض) causing the following present verb to be subjunctive after فَاء السَّبَبِيَّة.
b: أَلَا تَدْنُو فَتُبْصِرَ مَا قَدْ حَدَّثُوكَ — فَتُبْصِرَ is subjunctive after an offer.

f: What restriction does Ibn Hishām place on the "request" (الطلب) that licenses subjunctive after فَاء السَّبَبِيَّة?
b: The request must be expressed by a verb. Nouns functioning as commands (e.g. نَزَالَ, صَهْ) do not qualify according to the preferred view.

f: After what preceding context is أَنْ obligatorily omitted after وَاوُ الْمَعِيَّة?
b: After pure negation (النفي المحض) or a verbal request (الطلب بالفعل).

f: Give a Qurʾānic example of وَاوُ الْمَعِيَّة after pure negation requiring an omitted أَنْ.
b: ﴿وَلَمَّا يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا مِنْكُمْ وَيَعْلَمَ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾ — يَعْلَمَ is subjunctive with an omitted أَنْ.

f: Give a Qurʾānic example of وَاوُ الْمَعِيَّة after a verbal request requiring an omitted أَنْ.
b: ﴿يَا لَيْتَنَا نُرَدُّ وَلَا نُكَذِّبَ بِآيَاتِ رَبِّنَا وَنَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ (reading of Ḥamzah, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Ḥafṣ).

f: How is the verb interpreted in the sentence: لَا تَأْكُلِ السَّمَكَ وَتَشْرَبَ اللَّبَنَ?
b: تَشْرَبَ is subjunctive if the meaning is: Do not combine eating fish with drinking milk.

f: How is the verb interpreted in the sentence: لَا تَأْكُلِ السَّمَكَ وَتَشْرَبِ اللَّبَنَ? (jussive reading)
b: تَشْرَبْ is jussive if the meaning is: Do not eat fish, and do not drink milk.

f: How is the verb interpreted in the sentence: لَا تَأْكُلِ السَّمَكَ وَتَشْرَبُ اللَّبَنَ? (indicative reading)
b: تَشْرَبُ is indicative if only eating fish is prohibited while drinking milk remains permitted.

f: When is a present verb jussive after a request (الطلب) without فَاء?
b: When the فَاء is omitted and the speaker intends the verb to express the result (الجزاء) of the request.

f: Give a Qurʾānic example of a present verb becoming jussive after a request because فَاء is omitted.
b: ﴿قُلْ تَعَالَوْا أَتْلُ﴾ — أَتْلُ is jussive because it is the consequence of the command تَعَالَوْا.

f: What condition must be satisfied for a present verb after a prohibition to be jussive as the result of the prohibition?
b: The sentence must accept the substitution of إِنْ لَا ("if not"), making the prohibition function like a conditional.

f: Give an example where a present verb is jussive after a prohibition because the conditional meaning is valid.
b: لَا تَدْنُ مِنَ الْأَسَدِ تَسْلَمْ — meaning: If you do not approach the lion, you will be safe.

f: Why is the verb not jussive in a sentence like: لَا تَدْنُ مِنَ الْأَسَدِ يَأْكُلُكَ?
b: Because the conditional interpretation (إِنْ لَا) is not valid; the second verb is not the intended consequence of obeying the prohibition.

f: Which particles each jussive a single present verb (تجزم فعلًا واحدًا)?
b: They are: لَمْ, لَمَّا, لَامُ الْأَمْرِ, and لَا النَّاهِيَة (in addition to the special case of a request expressing a conditional meaning).

f: Give examples of the jussive particles لَمْ, لَمَّا, لَامُ الْأَمْرِ, and لَا النَّاهِيَة.
b: لَمْ يَلِدْ; وَلَمَّا يَقْضِ; لِيُنْفِقْ

f: Which particles make two present verbs jussive (تجزم فعلين)?
b: إِنْ، إِذْمَا، أَيْنَ، أَنَّى، أَيَّانَ، مَتَى، مَهْمَا، مَنْ، مَا، حَيْثُمَا.

f: What are the two verbs called in a conditional sentence introduced by a particle that jussives two verbs?
b: The first is the verb of the condition (فعل الشرط), and the second is the answer/result (جواب الشرط أو الجزاء).

f: Give a Qurʾānic example of a conditional particle jussiving two verbs.
b: ﴿إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ﴾ — both verbs are jussive.

f: Give another Qurʾānic example of a conditional particle jussiving two verbs.
b: ﴿مَا نَنْسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ أَوْ نُنْسِهَا نَأْتِ بِخَيْرٍ مِنْهَا﴾.

f: When must the answer of a conditional sentence be preceded by فَاء?
b: When it is not suitable to follow the conditional particle directly (i.e., it cannot function as a plain jussive answer).

f: Give a Qurʾānic example where the answer of the condition is introduced by فَاء.
b: ﴿وَإِنْ يَمْسَسْكَ بِخَيْرٍ فَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾.

f: When must the answer of a conditional sentence be preceded by إِذَا الفُجَائِيَّة?
b: When the answer is one of the constructions that require إِذَا الفُجَائِيَّة rather than a simple jussive verb.

f: Give a Qurʾānic example where the answer of the condition is introduced by إِذَا الفُجَائِيَّة.
b: ﴿وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ إِذَا هُمْ يَقْنَطُونَ﴾.

f: What is the grammatical rule for jussive (جزم) of a present verb that follows a request (الطَّلَب) without فَاء, and what conditions must be met?
b: A present verb becomes majzūm (jussive) when it follows a request (such as a command, prohibition, question, wish, etc.) without the conjunction فَاء, provided that the verb is intended as the result (جَزَاء) of the request. The request therefore carries the meaning of a conditional clause. Example: ﴿قُلْ تَعَالَوْا أَتْلُ﴾ ("Come, and I shall recite..."), meaning: "If you come, I shall recite." The verb أَتْلُ is jussive by deleting its final weak letter.

f: Give examples of present verbs becoming jussive as the result of a preceding request (الطَّلَب).
b: Examples include: ائْتِنِي أُكْرِمْكَ ("Come to me and I will honour you."); هَلْ تَأْتِينِي أُحَدِّثْكَ؟ ("Will you come to me so that I may speak to you?"); لَا تَكْفُرْ تَدْخُلِ الْجَنَّةَ ("Do not disbelieve and you will enter Paradise."). In each case the second verb is jussive because it is the result of the first request.

f: Does a present verb become jussive after a negative statement or an affirmative statement?
b: No. If what precedes is merely a negative statement or an affirmative statement, the following present verb remains indicative (مرفوع). Examples: مَا تَأْتِينَا تُحَدِّثُنَا ("You do not come to us and speak to us.") and أَنْتَ تَأْتِينَا تُحَدِّثُنَا ("You come to us and speak to us."). In both cases تُحَدِّثُنَا must be indicative.

f: Why is the verb يَغْفِرْ in the verse ﴿تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ... يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ﴾ jussive?
b: In ﴿تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَتُجَاهِدُونَ... يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ﴾, the verbs تُؤْمِنُونَ and تُجَاهِدُونَ carry the meaning of an imperative ("Believe" and "Strive"), so يَغْفِرْ is the jussive result of that implied command, not the result of the preceding interrogative expression.

f: When does a present verb following a request not become jussive?
b: If the following verb is not intended as the result of the request but merely describes or qualifies something, it remains indicative. Example: ﴿خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً تُطَهِّرُهُمْ﴾. Here تُطَهِّرُهُمْ describes the charity ("a charity that purifies them") rather than expressing the consequence of taking it.

f: Why can the verb يُحِبُّ in the sentence ائْتِنِي بِرَجُلٍ يُحِبُّ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ not be jussive?
b: In ائْتِنِي بِرَجُلٍ يُحِبُّ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ, the verb يُحِبُّ is a descriptive relative clause modifying رَجُلٍ ("a man who loves Allah and His Messenger"), not the consequence of bringing the man. Therefore it cannot be jussive.

f: What condition must be satisfied for a verb after a prohibition (النَّهْي) to become jussive as its result?
b: The sentence must accept an equivalent conditional construction with إِنْ لَا while preserving the meaning. Examples: لَا تَكْفُرْ تَدْخُلِ الْجَنَّةَ ("If you do not disbelieve, you will enter Paradise.") and لَا تَدْنُ مِنَ الْأَسَدِ تَسْلَمْ ("If you do not approach the lion, you will be safe.").

f: Give examples where a verb after a prohibition cannot be jussive and explain why.
b: Examples include لَا تَكْفُرْ تَدْخُلُ النَّارَ and لَا تَدْنُ مِنَ الْأَسَدِ يَأْكُلُكَ. They cannot be interpreted with إِنْ لَا, so the second verb is not a conditional result and therefore cannot be jussive.

f: Why is تَسْتَكْثِرُ in the verse ﴿وَلَا تَمْنُنْ تَسْتَكْثِرُ﴾ indicative rather than jussive?
b: The phrase does not mean "If you do not give, you will seek more." Rather, تَسْتَكْثِرُ functions as a circumstantial clause (حال): "Do not give while seeking more in return." Therefore the verb is indicative rather than the jussive answer to the prohibition.

f: How did Ibn Hishām explain the jussive reading تَسْتَكْثِرْ reported from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī?
b: He mentioned three possible explanations: (1) it is a substitute for تَمْنُنْ, meaning "Do not regard what you give as abundant."; (2) it reflects pausal pronunciation carried into connected speech; or (3) the final consonant was made silent to match the endings of neighbouring Qurʾānic verses.

f: What is the particle لَمْ, and what are its grammatical effects?
b: لَمْ is a particle that negates a present verb, changes its meaning to the past, and makes the verb jussive. Examples: لَمْ يَقُمْ, لَمْ يَقْعُدْ, ﴿لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ﴾.

f: What are the similarities between لَمْ and لَمَّا?
b: Both are particles that: (1) are used only with present verbs; (2) make the present verb jussive; (3) shift its meaning to the past; and (4) are indeclinable particles.

f: How does لَمَّا differ from لَمْ?
b: لَمَّا usually indicates that the negation continues up to the present and often implies that the action is still expected later. Example: ﴿بَلْ لَمَّا يَذُوقُوا عَذَابِ﴾ ("They have not yet tasted My punishment."). لَمْ merely negates a past occurrence without implying future expectation.

f: Can a verb be omitted after لَمَّا? Can it be omitted after لَمْ?
b: Yes. After لَمَّا, the verb may be omitted when understood from context. Example: هَلْ دَخَلْتَ الْبَلَدَ؟ — قَارَبْتُهَا وَلَمَّا ("I came near it, but not yet [entered]."). This omission is not permitted after لَمْ.

f: Can لَمَّا be preceded by a conditional particle?
b: No. Expressions such as إِنْ لَمَّا تَقُمْ are not permitted. By contrast, إِنْ لَمْ تَقُمْ is valid.

f: What is لَامُ الطَّلَبِ (the imperative lām), and what meanings can it express?
b: لَامُ الطَّلَبِ is a particle that makes the present verb jussive. It may express a command, as in ﴿لِيُنْفِقْ ذُو سَعَةٍ مِنْ سَعَتِهِ﴾, or a supplication, as in ﴿لِيَقْضِ عَلَيْنَا رَبُّكَ﴾.

f: What is لَا الطَّلَبِيَّة (the prohibitive لَا), and what meanings can it express?
b: لَا الطَّلَبِيَّة is the prohibitive لَا, which makes the present verb jussive. It may express prohibition, as in ﴿لَا تُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ﴾, or supplication, as in ﴿لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَا﴾.

f: Which particles make two present verbs (فِعْلَانِ مُضَارِعَانِ) jussive (مَجْزُوم), and what are they called?
b: There are eleven conditional particles (أَدَوَاتُ الشَّرْطِ) that make two present verbs jussive: إِنْ، أَيْنَمَا، أَيٌّ، مَنْ، مَا، مَهْمَا، مَتَى، أَيَّانَ، حَيْثُمَا، إِذْمَا، أَنَّى. The first verb is called فِعْلُ الشَّرْطِ (the conditional verb), and the second is called جَوَابُ الشَّرْطِ or جَزَاءُ الشَّرْطِ (the apodosis or result clause).

f: How does the conditional particle إِنْ function, and give an example?
b: إِنْ is a conditional particle that makes both the conditional verb and its answer jussive. Example: ﴿إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ﴾ — "If He wills, He will remove you." Both يَشَأْ and يُذْهِبْ are jussive.

f: How does the conditional particle أَيْنَمَا function, and give an example?
b: أَيْنَمَا means "wherever." It makes both verbs jussive. Example: ﴿أَيْنَمَا تَكُونُوا يُدْرِكْكُمُ الْمَوْتُ﴾ — "Wherever you may be, death will reach you."

f: How does the conditional particle أَيٌّ function, and give an example?
b: أَيٌّ (when used conditionally and followed by مَا) means "whichever." Example: ﴿أَيًّا مَا تَدْعُوا فَلَهُ الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى﴾ — "Whichever Name you call upon, to Him belong the Most Beautiful Names."

f: How does the conditional particle مَنْ function, and give an example?
b: مَنْ means "whoever." It makes both verbs jussive. Example: ﴿مَنْ يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا يُجْزَ بِهِ﴾ — "Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it."

f: How does the conditional particle مَا function, and give an example?
b: مَا means "whatever." It makes both verbs jussive. Example: ﴿وَمَا تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ يَعْلَمْهُ اللَّهُ﴾ — "Whatever good you do, Allah knows it."

f: How does the conditional particle مَهْمَا function, and give an example?
b: مَهْمَا means "whatever." Example: مَهْمَا تَأْمُرِي الْقَلْبَ يَفْعَلْ — "Whatever you command the heart, it will do." Both verbs are jussive.

f: How does the conditional particle مَتَى function, and give an example?
b: مَتَى means "whenever." Example: مَتَى أَضَعِ الْعِمَامَةَ تَعْرِفُونِي — "Whenever I remove my turban, you will recognize me."

f: How does the conditional particle أَيَّانَ function, and give an example?
b: أَيَّانَ means "whenever" or "at whatever time." Example: فَأَيَّانَ مَا تَعْدِلْ بِهِ الرِّيحُ تَنْزِلْ — "Wherever the wind carries it, it comes down."

f: How does the conditional particle حَيْثُمَا function, and give an example?
b: حَيْثُمَا means "wherever." Example: حَيْثُمَا تَسْتَقِمْ يُقَدِّرْ لَكَ اللَّهُ نَجَاحًا — "Wherever you remain upright, Allah will decree success for you."

f: How does the conditional particle إِذْمَا function, and give an example?
b: إِذْمَا is a conditional particle meaning "whenever." Example: وَإِنَّكَ إِذْمَا تَأْتِ مَا أَنْتَ آمِرٌ بِهِ تَلْقَ مِنْ إِيَّاهُ تَأْمُرُ آتِيًا — "Whenever you do what you command, you will find those whom you command complying."

f: How does the conditional particle أَنَّى function, and give an example?
b: أَنَّى means "wherever" or "however." Example: فَأَصْبَحْتُ أَنَّى تَأْتِهَا تَسْتَجِرْ بِهَا تَجِدْ — "Wherever you come to it seeking protection, you will find it."

f: What are the names of the two verbs governed by a conditional particle (أَدَاةُ الشَّرْطِ)?
b: The first jussive verb is called فِعْلُ الشَّرْطِ (the conditional verb), while the second jussive verb is called جَوَابُ الشَّرْطِ or جَزَاءُ الشَّرْطِ (the answer or result clause).

f: When must the answer to a conditional sentence (جَوَابُ الشَّرْطِ) be preceded by the particle فَاء?
b: The answer must be introduced by فَاءُ الْجَوَابِ whenever it is not suitable to function directly as a conditional answer. This occurs when the answer is: (1) a nominal sentence (جُمْلَةٌ اسْمِيَّةٌ), (2) a verbal sentence beginning with a command, prohibition, request, or other imperative expression, (3) headed by a frozen (non-conjugating) verb (فِعْلٌ جَامِدٌ), (4) negated by لَنْ or مَا, (5) introduced by قَدْ, or (6) introduced by a future particle such as سَ or سَوْفَ.

f: Give examples of conditional answers that require فَاءُ الْجَوَابِ.
b: Examples include: ﴿وَإِنْ يَمْسَسْكَ بِخَيْرٍ فَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ (nominal sentence); ﴿قُلْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ اللَّهَ فَاتَّبِعُونِي﴾ (imperative); ﴿إِنْ تَرَنِ أَنَا أَقَلَّ مِنْكَ مَالًا وَوَلَدًا فَعَسَى رَبِّي﴾ (frozen verb عَسَى); ﴿وَمَا يَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَلَنْ يُكْفَرُوهُ﴾ (negated by لَنْ); ﴿فَسَوْفَ نُؤْتِيهِ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾ (preceded by سَوْفَ).

f: When may the answer to a conditional sentence be introduced by إِذَا الْفُجَائِيَّة instead of فَاء?
b: If the answer is a nominal sentence, it may be introduced by إِذَا الْفُجَائِيَّة ("suddenly"). Example: ﴿وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ إِذَا هُمْ يَقْنَطُونَ﴾ — "If a calamity befalls them because of what their hands have sent forth, suddenly they despair."

f: What is the definition of an indefinite noun (النَّكِرَةُ) according to Ibn Hishām?
b: An indefinite noun (النَّكِرَةُ) is a noun that applies generally to any member of an existing genus or a mentally conceivable genus. Existing genus: رَجُلٌ ("a man"), which applies to any individual man. Conceivable genus: شَمْسٌ ("a sun"), whose genus could apply to multiple individuals if they existed, even though only one exists in reality.

f: Why does Ibn Hishām classify شَمْسٌ as an indefinite noun although only one sun exists?
b: Because indefiniteness depends on how the word was coined, not on the number of existing individuals. The noun شَمْسٌ was coined as the name of a genus, not as a proper name like زَيْدٌ. If multiple suns existed, the same noun would naturally apply to all of them.

f: Into how many categories are nouns divided with respect to definiteness (التَّعْرِيفُ وَالتَّنْكِيرُ)?
b: Nouns are divided into two categories: النَّكِرَةُ (indefinite nouns) and الْمَعْرِفَةُ (definite nouns). Indefiniteness is the original state, while definiteness is secondary.

f: Into how many categories are definite nouns (الْمَعَارِفُ) divided according to Ibn Hishām?
b: Definite nouns are divided into six categories (سِتَّةُ أَقْسَامٍ), beginning with the pronoun (الضَّمِيرُ).

f: What is the definition of a pronoun (الضَّمِيرُ)?
b: A pronoun (الضَّمِيرُ) is a definite noun that refers to a speaker (مُتَكَلِّم), an addressee (مُخَاطَب), or an absent person or thing (غَائِب).

f: Into what two major categories are Arabic pronouns (الضَّمَائِرُ) divided?
b: Arabic pronouns are divided into hidden (مُسْتَتِر) and overt (بَارِز) pronouns.

f: What is the difference between a obligatorily hidden pronoun (ضَمِيرٌ مُسْتَتِرٌ وُجُوبًا) and a permissibly hidden pronoun (ضَمِيرٌ مُسْتَتِرٌ جَوَازًا)?
b: An obligatorily hidden pronoun must remain unexpressed, such as in أَقُومُ ("I stand") and نَقُومُ ("We stand"). A permissibly hidden pronoun may remain hidden, such as in زَيْدٌ يَقُومُ, where the hidden pronoun refers back to زَيْدٌ.

f: Into what two categories are overt pronouns (الضَّمَائِرُ الْبَارِزَةُ) divided?
b: Overt pronouns are divided into attached pronouns (مُتَّصِلَة), such as تَاءُ قُمْتُ, كَافُ أَكْرَمَكَ, and هَاءُ غُلَامُهُ, and detached pronouns (مُنْفَصِلَة), such as أَنَا، هُوَ، إِيَّايَ.

f: When is it permissible to use a detached pronoun instead of an attached pronoun?
b: The rule is not to separate (detach) a pronoun when attachment is possible, except in certain specific constructions mentioned by Ibn Hishām, such as سَلْنِيهِ (where separation is less preferred) and ظَنَنْتُكَهُ or كُنْتُهُ (where separation is preferred according to the grammarians).

f: What is the first category of definite nouns (المعارف), and why is it mentioned first?
b: The first category is the pronoun (الضَّمِير). It is mentioned first because it is considered the most definite (أَعْرَفُ المَعَارِفِ) of the six categories of definite nouns.

f: What is the definition of a pronoun (الضَّمِير)?
b: A pronoun is a word that indicates a speaker (مُتَكَلِّم), an addressee (مُخَاطَب), or an absent person or thing (غَائِب).Examples:• Speaker: أَنَا• Addressee: أَنْتَ• Absent: هُوَ

f: Into what two categories are pronouns divided?
b: Pronouns are divided into:1. Hidden (ضَمِيرٌ مُسْتَتِرٌ) — having no explicit form in speech.2. Overt (ضَمِيرٌ بَارِزٌ) — having an explicit spoken form.

f: What is an overt pronoun (الضَّمِيرُ البَارِزُ)? Give an example.
b: An overt pronoun is one that has an explicit form in pronunciation.Example: the تَاءُ الفَاعِلِ in قُمْتُ.

f: What is a hidden pronoun (الضَّمِيرُ المُسْتَتِرُ)? Give an example.
b: A hidden pronoun is one that has no explicit spoken form but is understood.Example: the hidden subject in قُمْ ("Stand!"), whose subject is understood as أَنْتَ.

f: Into what two categories is the hidden pronoun divided?
b: The hidden pronoun is divided into:1. Obligatorily hidden (وَاجِبُ الِاسْتِتَارِ).2. Permissibly hidden (جَائِزُ الِاسْتِتَارِ).

f: What is an obligatorily hidden pronoun (الضَّمِيرُ الوَاجِبُ الِاسْتِتَارِ)?
b: It is a hidden pronoun whose place cannot be taken by an explicit noun.Examples are the subjects of imperfect verbs beginning with:• أَ: أَقُومُ• نَ: نَقُومُ• تَ: تَقُومُThus one cannot say: أَقُومُ زَيْدٌ or نَقُومُ عَمْرٌو.

f: What is a permissibly hidden pronoun (الضَّمِيرُ الجَائِزُ الِاسْتِتَارِ)?
b: It is a hidden pronoun whose place may be taken by an explicit noun.Example:زَيْدٌ يَقُومُ → One may also say زَيْدٌ يَقُومُ غُلَامُهُ.

f: Into what two categories is the overt pronoun divided?
b: Into:1. Attached (مُتَّصِل).2. Detached (مُنْفَصِل).

f: What is an attached pronoun (الضَّمِيرُ المُتَّصِلُ)?
b: An attached pronoun is one that cannot stand independently, such as the تَاء in قُمْتُ.

f: What is a detached pronoun (الضَّمِيرُ المُنْفَصِلُ)?
b: A detached pronoun is one that can stand independently, such as أَنَا، أَنْتَ، هُوَ.

f: Into what categories are attached pronouns divided according to grammatical function?
b: Attached pronouns are divided into:1. Nominative (مَرْفُوع).2. Accusative (مَنْصُوب).3. Genitive (مَخْفُوض).

f: Give examples of nominative, accusative, and genitive attached pronouns.
b: Nominative: قُمْتُ (the تَاء is the subject).Accusative: أَكْرَمَكَ (the كَاف is the direct object).Genitive: غُلَامُهُ (the هَاء is the genitive by possession).

f: Into what categories are detached pronouns divided according to grammatical function?
b: Detached pronouns are divided into:1. Nominative only.2. Accusative only.There are no detached genitive pronouns.

f: List the detached nominative pronouns.
b: أَنَا، نَحْنُ، أَنْتَ، أَنْتِ، أَنْتُمَا، أَنْتُمْ، أَنْتُنَّ، هُوَ، هِيَ، هُمَا، هُمْ، هُنَّ.

f: List the detached accusative pronouns.
b: إِيَّايَ، إِيَّانَا، إِيَّاكَ، إِيَّاكِ، إِيَّاكُمَا، إِيَّاكُمْ، إِيَّاكُنَّ، إِيَّاهُ، إِيَّاهَا، إِيَّاهُمَا، إِيَّاهُمْ، إِيَّاهُنَّ.

f: Can detached nominative pronouns be used in the accusative, or detached accusative pronouns in the nominative?
b: No. Each set is restricted to its grammatical function. Thus one says:أَنَا مُؤْمِنٌ (not إِيَّايَ مُؤْمِنٌ).إِيَّاكَ أَكْرَمْتُ (not أَنْتَ أَكْرَمْتُ).

f: What is the general rule regarding the use of attached and detached pronouns?
b: Whenever an attached pronoun is possible, it must be used, and one should not replace it with a detached pronoun.

f: Give examples where detached pronouns are required because attachment is impossible.
b: Examples:مَا قَامَ إِلَّا أَنَامَا أَكْرَمْتُ إِلَّا إِيَّاكَThe particle إِلَّا prevents the use of attached pronouns.

f: What is the first exception in which a detached pronoun may be used even though an attached pronoun is possible?
b: When the pronoun is the second of two pronouns, the first is more definite, and it is not nominative.Examples:سَلْنِيهِ / سَلْنِي إِيَّاهُخِلْتُكَهُ

f: Why is the first pronoun in expressions such as سَلْنِيهِ considered more definite than the second?
b: Because the order of definiteness among pronouns is:Speaker (المُتَكَلِّم) > Addressee (المُخَاطَب) > Absent (الغَائِب).

f: What is the second exception allowing separation of a pronoun?
b: When the pronoun is the predicate (خبر) of كَانَ or one of its sisters, whether preceded by another pronoun or not.Examples:الصَّدِيقُ كُنْتُهُ / كُنْتُ إِيَّاهُالصَّدِيقُ كَانَهُ زَيْدٌ

f: According to Ibn Hishām, which form is generally preferred: attachment or separation?
b: In non-mental verbs (e.g., سَلْنِيهِ، أَعْطِنِيهِ), attachment is preferred. With mental verbs and with كَانَ, scholars differed. The majority preferred separation in many of these cases, while Ibn Mālik often preferred attachment.

f: What is the definition of a proper noun (العَلَم)?
b: A proper noun is a noun assigned to a specific individual and not applicable to others resembling it.

f: Into what two categories are proper nouns divided according to what they denote?
b: They are divided into:1. Personal proper nouns (عَلَمُ شَخْصٍ) — e.g., زَيْدٌ.2. Generic proper nouns (عَلَمُ جِنْسٍ) — e.g., أُسَامَةُ (lion).

f: What is a generic proper noun (عَلَمُ الجِنْسِ)? Give examples.
b: It is a proper noun denoting the essence of an entire species rather than one individual.Examples:أُسَامَةُ (lion)ثُعَالَةُ (fox)ذُؤَالَةُ (wolf).

f: Into what categories are proper nouns divided according to their structure?
b: Into:1. Simple (مُفْرَد).2. Compound (مُرَكَّب).

f: What are the three kinds of compound proper nouns?
b: 1. Genitive compound (تَرْكِيبُ إِضَافَة) — e.g., عَبْدُ اللَّهِ.2. Blended compound (تَرْكِيبُ مَزْج) — e.g., بَعْلَبَكَّ، سِيبَوَيْهِ.3. Sentential compound (تَرْكِيبُ إِسْنَاد) — e.g., شَابَ قَرْنَاهَا.

f: How are genitive compounds (المركب الإضافي) declined?
b: The first part is declined according to its grammatical role, while the second part is always genitive as the second term of an iḍāfah.

f: How are blended compounds (المركب المزجي) declined?
b: If not ending in ـوَيْهِ, they behave like diptotes: ḍammah in the nominative and fatḥah in both the accusative and genitive.If ending in ـوَيْهِ, such as سِيبَوَيْهِ, they are indeclinable on kasrah.

f: How are sentential compounds (المركب الإسنادي) treated grammatically?
b: They are quoted unchanged (محكيّ), and grammatical factors do not alter their original form.

f: Into what three categories are proper nouns divided according to usage?
b: Into:1. Name (اِسْم).2. Kunyah (كُنْيَة).3. Laqab (لَقَب).

f: What is a kunyah (كُنْيَة)?
b: A proper noun beginning with أَبُو or أُمُّ, such as:أَبُو بَكْرٍأَبُو عَمْرٍوأُمُّ كُلْثُومٍ

f: What is a laqab (لَقَب)?
b: A descriptive title that conveys praise or blame.Examples:زَيْنُ العَابِدِينَ (praise)قُفَّةٌ (blame).

f: What is an ism (اِسْم) in this classification?
b: A proper noun that is neither a kunyah nor a laqab, such as زَيْدٌ and عَمْرٌو.

f: When a personal name and a laqab occur together, what is the preferred order?
b: The personal name comes first, followed by the laqab.

f: When are the name and laqab treated as apposition (بدل أو عطف بيان)?
b: When:• Both are in iḍāfah.• The first is simple and the second is in iḍāfah.• The first is in iḍāfah and the second is simple.In these cases the laqab follows the grammatical case of the name.

f: If both the name and the laqab are simple nouns (e.g., زَيْدٌ قُفَّةٌ), what are the two grammatical opinions? Which does Ibn Hishām prefer?
b: The Kufans and al-Zajjāj allow:1. Apposition (الإِتْبَاع).2. Making the name an iḍāfah to the laqab (الإِضَافَة).Most Basrans require the iḍāfah. Ibn Hishām considers apposition stronger by analogy (أَقْيَس), although iḍāfah is more common in usage (أَكْثَر).

f: What is the third type of maʿrifah (definite noun)?
b: Ism al-Ishārah (اسم الإشارة), the demonstrative pronoun.

f: What demonstrative is used for the masculine singular?
b: ذا (dhā). Usually appears as هذا with هاء التنبيه.

f: What demonstratives are used for the feminine singular?
b: There are ten reported forms: ذي، ذهي، ذه، ذهْ، ذات، تي، تهي، تيه، تهْ، تا. The most common in usage is هذه.

f: Which feminine demonstrative form is considered the rarest?
b: ذات as a demonstrative.

f: What are the three uses of ذات?
b: (1) Meaning "owner/possessor" (e.g., ذات جمال), (2) meaning "the one which (التي)" in the dialect of Ṭayyiʾ, and (3) as a rare feminine demonstrative.

f: What are the demonstratives for the masculine dual?
b: ذان (nominative) and ذين (accusative/genitive).

f: What are the demonstratives for the feminine dual?
b: تان (nominative) and تين

f: What demonstrative is used for both masculine and feminine plurals?
b: أولاء (commonly هؤلاء when preceded by هاء التنبيه).

f: How are demonstratives divided according to the referent?
b: Into those referring to a singular, dual, and plural; each has masculine and feminine forms where applicable.

f: How is a demonstrative used for a nearby object?
b: It is used without the kāf (ك) of distance. هاء التنبيه (ها) may optionally precede it, e.g., هذا or ذا.

f: How is a demonstrative used for a distant object?
b: It must take the كاف البعد (ك), either alone (e.g., ذاك) or together with لام البعد (ل) (e.g., ذلك).

f: When is لام البعد prohibited?
b: In three cases: (1) with the dual (ذانك، تانك), (2) with the plural in the dialect that uses أولاء, and (3) whenever هاء التنبيه precedes the demonstrative (e.g., هذاك, not هذالك).

f: What is the fourth type of maʿrifah?
b: Ism al-Mawṣūl (الاسم الموصول), the relative pronoun.

f: What are the specific (specialized) relative pronouns?
b: الذي، التي، اللذان، اللتان، الذين، الأولى، اللائي، اللاتي.

f: How are اللذان and اللتان declined?
b: They take الألف in the nominative and الياء in the accusative and genitive.

f: How is الذين declined?
b: It remains with الياء in all grammatical cases.

f: Which tribes used الذون in the nominative?
b: Hudhayl (هذيل) and ʿAqīl (عقيل).

f: Which forms are used for the feminine plural relative pronoun?
b: اللائي and اللاتي, with the option of retaining or omitting the final ياء.

f: What are the common (shared) relative pronouns?
b: من، ما، أي، أل، ذو، ذا.

f: Why are these called common relative pronouns?
b: Because they can refer to the singular, dual, or plural, masculine or feminine, depending on context.

f: Under what condition is أل considered a relative pronoun rather than the definite article?
b: When it is attached to a clear descriptive adjective (وصف صريح) that is not a comparative (اسم التفضيل).

f: Which descriptive forms can take relative أل?
b: اسم الفاعل, اسم المفعول, and الصفة المشبهة (e.g., الضارب، المضروب، الحسن).

f: When is أل merely the definite article rather than a relative pronoun?
b: When attached to a noun (e.g., الرجل), a noun-like adjective (e.g., الصاحب), or a comparative adjective (e.g., الأفضل، الأعلى).

f: In whose dialect is ذو used as a relative pronoun?
b: The dialect of Ṭayyiʾ (طيء).

f: Under what condition is ذا considered a relative pronoun?
b: Only when preceded by ما or من used interrogatively, e.g., ماذا or من ذا.

f: Give an example of ذا functioning as a relative pronoun.
b: ماذا أنزل ربكم؟ = "What is it that your Lord sent down?" (ما الذي).

f: What is the grammatical analysis of ماذا in this usage?
b: It means ما الذي, where ذا functions as the relative pronoun.

f: What is the grammatical analysis of من ذا قالها؟
b: It means من الذي قالها؟, where ذا functions as the relative pronoun.

f: Can ذا be a relative pronoun without preceding ما or من?
b: No. In that case it is an ism al-ishārah (demonstrative pronoun) according to the Basran grammarians.

f: What was the Kufan argument for allowing ذا as a relative pronoun without ما or من?
b: They cited poetic evidence where ذا appeared to function as a relative pronoun.

f: How did Ibn Hishām answer the Kufan argument?
b: He interpreted ذا as a demonstrative pronoun, with the following clause functioning as a circumstantial clause (حال), not as a relative clause.

f: What evidence supports Ibn Hishām's interpretation that ذا is a demonstrative rather than a relative pronoun?
b: The presence of هاء التنبيه, which only enters demonstrative pronouns, not relative pronouns.

f: What two elements must every relative pronoun have?
b: A صلة (relative clause) and an عائد (resumptive pronoun).

f: What kinds of clauses can serve as the صلة?
b: (1) A declarative sentence containing a matching عائد, (2) a complete adverbial phrase (ظرف), or (3) a complete prepositional phrase (جار ومجرور) attached to an omitted استقر.

f: What is the عائد?
b: The pronoun inside the relative clause that refers back to the relative pronoun.

f: Can the عائد ever be omitted?
b: Yes, in certain cases, such as أيهم أشد and similar constructions mentioned by Ibn Hishām.

f: What forms can the ṣilah (صلة الموصول) of a relative pronoun take?
